title: Meter parts out of a feed chute with a two-stop escapement, keeping the red part back
instruction: Use the two stops on the feed chute to release, one at a time, every part ahead of the red one into the bin, then leave the red part in the chute with both hands off the stops.
context: Gravity feed chutes on assembly and machining lines hand out one part at a time with a two-stop escapement: one stop holds the queue while the other lets the first part go. Open both together and the whole queue runs out, past a marked part that should stay for the next batch.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (61 cm apart), x forward, y left; heights from the table top (74.75 cm above the floor). Chute: fixed dark grey steel, sloping 8 degrees down toward -y, centred at x = 24, inside 5.4 wide, 43 long, floor 0.5 thick; its floor's low end at y = -6, height 6, its high end at y = 36.6, height 12, closed; walls 0.5 thick, rising 3.4 above the floor; two steel legs, 6 x 2 cm, under it. A cover over it from 7 cm along the chute (measured from the low end) to the high end leaves a 3 cm slot along its centre, its underside 2.8 above the floor, 0.6 thick. Parts: six aluminium blocks, 5 x 5 cm and 2.5 tall, 150 g, each with a 2 x 0.8 x 1 cm nose low on its downhill face, nose against the block ahead, so neighbouring blocks stand 8 mm apart; five are silver and one is red; the first rests against the lower stop with its underside centre at y = 4.9, height 7.5. Lower stop: orange-painted steel, a 1.6 wide, 1 cm thick plate through the slot, at 8.5 cm along the chute, sprung shut (about 0.8 N at the pad, 4.3 N fully open) with its tip 1.2 above the floor; a see-saw lever on a pivot beside the chute joins it to a 5 x 5 cm pad, 1 thick, at x = 30.5, y = -8, top 9.8 high; pressing the pad down about 1.9 cm, to its stop, lifts the plate's tip clear of the blocks. Upper stop: blue-painted steel, a 1.6 wide, 5 mm thick pin at 13.9 cm along the chute, in the gap between the first and second blocks, sprung up (about 2 N, 5.6 N at the bottom) with its tip 3 above the floor; a 5 x 5 cm pad, 1 thick, at x = 30.5, y = 6.8, top 14.9 high; pressing the pad down 1.8 cm, to its stop, drops the tip to 1.2 above the floor. Bin: fixed blue low-friction plastic, centred at (24, -21.25), 12 wide and 29.5 long inside (y -6.5 to -36), 1 cm walls rising 4 above the table, 0.4 cm floor, with a 0.5 thick apron across its width sloping from 5 above the table at its +y wall down to its floor 9 cm along, under the chute's low end. Lots (one per trial): the red part is 2nd in the queue in A, 3rd in B, 4th in C, 5th in D, counting from the lower stop. The screenshot shows A.
scoring: Read at the end of the run (no early end). Terms. In the bin: underside centre inside its walls and between the table and 5.5 cm above it, still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s), stacked or tipped included. Red held: the red block's underside centre inside the chute's walls and at least 2.3 cm uphill of the lower stop's face. Passed: a part 1 cm or more beyond its place against the lower stop; it counts from then on. Pin down: the upper stop pressed 1 cm or more. Stops home: pin within 2 mm of its top, lever within 1 degree of shut. Hands clear: each gripper's fingertip midpoint 6 cm or more from the top centre of both pads and from every part. Score: 0 if any part passes without the pin down, if the red part ever passes, or if it isn't held at the end. 1.0 if the parts in the bin are exactly the parts ahead of the red one, every part has been still for the last 1 s, both stops are home and both hands clear. 0.15 if at least one part is in the bin and the count is one short, or exact with one of those last conditions missing. Otherwise 0. A part anywhere else counts for nothing. The parts keep their order in the chute, so a part in the bin is always one from ahead of the red one. The task's score is the mean over one trial of each lot; a fixed count that never reads the queue averages at most 0.29, and with no early end it can't stop itself at the right count. On real arms: count the bin's parts and check the red part from a top-down photo after the arms withdraw, and check from the video that the pin was down as each part went by.
reset_notes: Let both stops rest as sprung, hold the lower stop open, slide the parts back up through the chute's low end in the next lot's order (A, B, C, D in turn) with the upper stop held down to catch them, let the stops go, and let the parts rest nose to tail against the lower stop.
fidelity: Approximate. Parts slide on low friction (0.05) in place of rollers or a polished track, in the bin too; the stops are a rigid plate and pin on spring-return joints with no spring parts modelled, and their arms and links to the pads are shown only, with no contact; spring forces are typical of light hand-worked stops, not measured. Blocks' noses keep a gap for the upper pin; real chutes often use part shape or a wedge for the same job. Four fixed lots, chosen at the start.
